The decision to keep or shorten the tea-serving ceremony depends on several factors, including cultural traditions, the size of the family, the overall wedding schedule, and the couple’s vision for the event. This is a **major policy violation** that harms honest sellers and undermines trust in Amazon’s review system. 2. **Fake Positive Ratings** – Their 100% 5-star rating is likely inflated through this scheme (or other methods like fake accounts). Amazon’s algorithm detects suspicious review patterns, and this seller is likely **already flagged internally**. 3. **Free Item for No Reason** – They’re giving away products for free without any legitimate reason (like a promotion or loyalty program), which is a form of **deceptive marketing**. ### **What Should You Do Instead of Just Reporting?** Reporting alone may not be enough because: - The seller might **deny it** (e.g., claim it was a "mistake" or a "one-time promotion"). - Amazon’s enforcement is **inconsistent**—some sellers get away with it unless they’re caught in a larger pattern. #### **Recommended Steps (In Order):** 1. **Leave a 1-Star Review (But Be Careful!)** - Since you didn’t actually leave a review, you can’t report them for that—but you can **leave a negative review** on the product (not the seller) explaining: > *"Received a free item after claiming a fake review incentive. This seller is manipulating ratings—do not buy from them."* - **Why?** This exposes their scheme to other buyers without directly accusing them (which could get your review removed). 2. **Report Them to Amazon (But Use the Right Form)** - Go to the **seller’s page** → Click **"Report this listing"** → Select: - **"Suspicious activity"** (for fake reviews) - **"Violation of Amazon’s policies"** (for incentivizing reviews) - **Be specific**—mention the **Hotmail email, the fake note, and the free item** you received. 3. **Report to Amazon’s Seller Feedback Team (If Needed)** - If they keep selling, you can **submit a formal complaint** via: - [Amazon Seller Feedback Form](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/help.html?itemID=200441480) - **Tag them in a public forum** (e.g., Reddit’s r/AmazonSellers or Amazon’s Seller Central forums) to **crowdsource evidence**. 4. **Consider Reporting to the FTC (If in the U.S.)** - If this is part of a **larger pattern**, you can file a complaint with the [FTC](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/) for **deceptive business practices**. 5. **Warn Other Buyers (Anonymously)** - Post in **Amazon’s "Ask a Question" section** on their listing: > *"Warning: This seller offers ‘free items’ for fake reviews. Do not engage—they’re manipulating ratings."* - This helps **other buyers avoid them** without you getting personally involved. ### **Why This Works Better Than Just Reporting** - **Exposes their scheme** to more people (not just Amazon). - **Increases pressure** on Amazon to act (since they don’t want their platform associated with fake reviews). - **Protects other buyers** from falling for the same trick. ### **Final Verdict** **Yes, you should take action—but not just a simple report.** A **multi-step approach** (negative review + targeted report + public warning) will have the most impact. This seller is **exploiting Amazon’s system**, and exposing them helps keep the marketplace fair. Would you like help drafting the exact review or report message?
